knowledge:
- key_parameters: user_df=The prepared dataframe containing sample names and grouping factors (from convertCSV, convertESet, or convertSE) ;; plate_dims=List specifying the dimensions of the plate (e.g., list(8,12) for 8 rows and 12 columns) ;; nb_plates=The number of plates to fill ;; forbidden_wells=Character string of comma-separated well coordinates (e.g., "A1,A2,A3") that must not be filled ;; fixed_wells=Character string of comma-separated well coordinates (e.g., "B1,B2") reserved for quality control or standard samples ;; spatial_constraint=The spatial constraint pattern to prevent adjacent samples of the same group ("NS", "WE", "NSEW", or "None") ;; max_iteration=The maximum number of backtracking attempts to find a valid layout (default is 20)
- alternatives: none=No alternative packages or methods are mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use when designing high-throughput experiments (such as mass spectrometry or proteomics) that require distributing biological samples across one or multiple multi-well plates while minimizing batch/plate effects through randomized block design.
- pitfalls: incorrect_csv_format=CSV files must have sample names in the first column (or second column if rownames are present) ;; backtracking_failure=Complex constraints or small plate sizes relative to sample size can cause the algorithm to fail within the default 20 iterations, requiring an increase in iterations or relaxation of constraints ;; multiple_plates_indexing=When multiple plates are generated, wrapperWPM returns a list of dataframes, meaning the user must index the list (e.g., wpm_result[[1]]) before passing it to drawMap ;; shiny_app_unsaved_changes=Modifying parameters in the Shiny app's Parameters tab does not automatically update the Results tab; the user must click "start WPM" again to apply changes.

workflows.name: csv_to_plate_map
workflows.intent: Generate and visualize a randomized well-plate map starting from a CSV file containing sample metadata.
input: path-to-CSV-file (CSV file containing sample names in the first column and grouping factors in subsequent columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Convert the CSV file into the WPM-compatible dataframe format using convertCSV ;; 2. Run the randomization algorithm using wrapperWPM ;; 3. Visualize the generated plate map using drawMap ;; 4. Save the generated plot using ggplot2::ggsave
workflows.code:
imported_csv <- wpm::convertCSV("path-to-CSV-file")
wpm_result <- wpm::wrapperWPM(user_df = imported_csv$df_wpm,
            plate_dims = list(8,12),
            nb_plates = 1,
            forbidden_wells = "A1,A2,A3",
            fixed_wells = "B1,B2",
            spatial_constraint = "NS")
drawned_map <- wpm::drawMap(df = wpm_result,
        sample_gps = length(levels(as.factor(colData$Treatment))),
        gp_levels = gp_lvl <- levels(as.factor(colData$Treatment)),
        plate_lines = 8,
        plate_cols = 12,
        project_title = "my Project Title")
drawned_map
ggplot2::ggsave(
    filename = "my file name",
    plot = drawned_map,
    width = 10,
    height = 7,
    units = "in"
)

workflows.name: expressionset_to_plate_map
workflows.intent: Generate and visualize a randomized well-plate map starting from an ExpressionSet or MSnSet object.
input: my_MSnSet_object (An MSnSet or ExpressionSet object containing sample expression data and metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Convert the ExpressionSet/MSnSet object into the WPM-compatible dataframe format using convertESet, specifying the grouping factor ;; 2. Run the randomization algorithm using wrapperWPM ;; 3. Visualize the generated plate map using drawMap
workflows.code:
sample_names <- c("s1","s2","s3","s4", "s5")
M <- matrix(NA, nrow = 4, ncol = 5)
colnames(M) <- sample_names
rownames(M) <- paste0("id", LETTERS[1:4])
pd <- data.frame(Environment = rep_len(LETTERS[1:3], 5),
                 Category = rep_len(1:2, 5), row.names = sample_names)
rownames(pd) <- colnames(M)
my_MSnSet_object <- MSnbase::MSnSet(exprs = M,pData =  pd)
df <- wpm::convertESet(my_MSnSet_object, "Environment")
wpm_result <- wpm::wrapperWPM(user_df = df,
            plate_dims = list(8,12),
            nb_plates = 1,
            forbidden_wells = "A1,A2,A3",
            fixed_wells = "B1,B2",
            spatial_constraint = "NS")
numberOfThePlate <- 1
drawned_map <- wpm::drawMap(df = wpm_result[[numberOfThePlate]],
        sample_gps = length(levels(as.factor(pd$Environment))),
        gp_levels = gp_lvl <- levels(as.factor(pd$Environment)),
        plate_lines = 8,
        plate_cols = 12,
        project_title = "my Project Title")
drawned_map

workflows.name: summarizedexperiment_to_plate_map
workflows.intent: Generate and visualize a randomized well-plate map starting from a SummarizedExperiment object.
input: se (A SummarizedExperiment object containing sample assays and colData metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Convert the SummarizedExperiment object into the WPM-compatible dataframe format using convertSE, specifying the grouping factor ;; 2. Run the randomization algorithm using wrapperWPM ;; 3. Visualize the generated plate map using drawMap
workflows.code:
nrows <- 200
ncols <- 6
counts <- matrix(runif(nrows * ncols, 1, 1e4), nrows)
colData <- data.frame(Treatment=rep(c("ChIP", "Input"), 3),
                      row.names=LETTERS[1:6])
se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(assays=list(counts=counts),
                                                 colData=colData)
df <- wpm::convertSE(se, "Treatment")
wpm_result <- wpm::wrapperWPM(user_df = df,
            plate_dims = list(8,12),
            nb_plates = 1,
            forbidden_wells = "A1,A2,A3",
            fixed_wells = "B1,B2",
            spatial_constraint = "NS")
drawned_map <- wpm::drawMap(df = wpm_result,
        sample_gps = length(levels(as.factor(colData$Treatment))),
        gp_levels = gp_lvl <- levels(as.factor(colData$Treatment)),
        plate_lines = 8,
        plate_cols = 12,
        project_title = "my Project Title")
drawned_map
